name: West Ridge

pitch_detail.notes: Start up the white-streaked, S-shaped crack that passes a tree; the 5.8 is a few face moves about halfway up, and the pitch belays on a ledge just left of the crest. Above, easy fifth-class blocks and some tree-thrashing lead along the ridge to a big ledge beside a boulder. With a long rope the two pitches link; the lower crack seeps and can be wet.

A sustained splitter hand crack on excellent rock climbs to a tree; from there move right and continue to the next ledge. The belay is built on gear (a #1 cam fits at the stance). Some rate the crack closer to 5.8 for how long it keeps going.

The technical crux: a steep, awkward pair of parallel cracks that flare into a short dihedral. It is pumpy but there are rests, and small cams protect it well. Grades given range from 5.8 to 5.9-. After the cracks, traverse left onto the face to a ledge with a tree belay; long slings help, as rope drag builds from the traverse.

Climb back up from the tree to regain the ridge. The more direct line starts with a hard layback and eases quickly but is sparsely protected; the alternative is a short, awkward fourth-class traverse that adds rope drag. Easy fourth class then leads to a belay at the base of the next splitter.

Follow the 5.6 splitter up mostly fourth-class ridge, then make an exposed traverse around the right side of a gendarme. Rope drag is the main problem on this long pitch: extend placements before the traverse, or stop short of the gendarme if the rope is dragging badly.
Stem and jam straight up a pair of parallel cracks, taking solid gear, to a good belay ledge below the final wall. A clean, enjoyable pitch that sets up the widening crack of the last lead.

A crack that widens to 4–6 inches leads to left-trending, exposed 5.8 face moves on a blank slab before reaching a jug and the ridge top. The face section is widely treated as the mental crux: protection is small and sparse, so carry wires and the smallest cams (a 0.2-size cam is valuable here) and climb it carefully.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 1 of 2, about 30 m, to a ledge. Downclimb from the ledge to the next anchors.
rappel_detail.station: From the summit, downclimb a few hundred feet of easy terrain until you are below the North Face of Burgundy Spire; the rappel slings on horns are plain to see. Anchors are plentiful on this descent.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 2 of 2, about 20 m, to the ground in the gully beneath Burgundy Col.
rappel_detail.station: The next anchors, reached by downclimbing from the ledge.

rappels: Downclimb a few hundred feet northeast from the summit, then 2 rappels, about 30 m and 20 m, down to the gully beneath Burgundy Col
descent_text: From the summit, downclimb easier terrain for a few hundred feet, then make two rappels — 30m and 20m — down into the gully beneath Burgundy Col, downclimbing sections between the rappel anchors. From the gully, follow the climbers' trail back down past the bench camp, cross Early Winters Creek, and finish with a short climb back up to the highway pullout.
approach: Follow the shared Wine Spires trail: boot path down talus to Early Winters Creek, cross on a log, then climb steeply up the timbered rib north of Burgundy Creek to the ~6,500 ft basin/camp (roughly 2 hours from the car). Paisano Pinnacle's West Ridge route starts lower than Burgundy Spire's and is commonly linked with Burgundy Spire's North Face in one long car-to-car day; fresh water is reported from a spring near the camp bench.
overview: The West Ridge climbs the crest of Paisano Pinnacle in 7-8 pitches of sustained, high-quality 5.8+ hand and finger cracks with big comfortable belay ledges, widely regarded as one of the best moderate alpine rock routes at Washington Pass.
beta: A hidden-gem moderate that has become cleaner and more popular over the years. The line rambles up cracks and the ridge crest with sustained mid-fifth-class climbing throughout; the crux comes about halfway up, on pitch 4, on a short section of steep twin finger cracks, and the final pitch is an exposed, runout 5.8 face regarded by many parties as the route's real ("mental") crux. Often camped for and combined with the North Face of Burgundy Spire for a ~12-13 pitch link-up day.
gear: Small cam (~0.2 in) for the final pitch
Two ropes capable of 30m rappels (or a single 60m)
face: West ridge crest of Paisano Pinnacle
